In [[geometry]], the '''deltoidal icositetrahedron''' (or '''trapezoidal icositetrahedron''', '''tetragonal icosikaitetrahedron''',<ref name="conway">{{cite book
 | first1 = John H. | last1 = Conway | author1-link = John Horton Conway
 | first2 = Heidi | last2 = Burgiel
 | first3 = Chaim | last3 = Goodman-Strauss
 | title = The Symmetries of Things
 | title-link = The Symmetries of Things
 | year = 2008
 | publisher = AK Peters
 | isbn = 978-1-56881-220-5
 | page = [https://books.google.com/books?id=Drj1CwAAQBAJ&pg=PA286 286]
}}</ref> '''tetragonal trisoctahedron''',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://etc.usf.edu/clipart/keyword/forms|title = Keyword: "forms" &#124; ClipArt ETC}}</ref> '''strombic icositetrahedron''') is a [[Catalan solid]].

== Description ==
[[File:Deltoidal icositetrahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of a deltoidal icositetrahedron]]
A deltoidal icositetrahedron is a [[Catalan solid]] with 24 sides that are [[Kite (geometry)|kites]]. All of its faces are [[Congruence (geometry)|congruent]], each has three interior angles approximately 81.6 degrees and one angle 115.3 degrees. The [[dihedral angle]] between every two kites is 138.1 degrees. The deltoidal icositetrahedron has 48 edges, and 26 vertices &ndash; eight vertices surrounded by three kites and eighteen vertices by four kites. Its [[dual polyhedron]] is the [[rhombicuboctahedron]], an [[Archimedean solid]].<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Williams | first = Robert | authorlink = Robert Williams (geometer)
 | year = 1979
 | title = The Geometrical Foundation of Natural Structure: A Source Book of Design
 | publisher = Dover Publications, Inc.
 | url = https://archive.org/details/geometricalfound00will/page/81
 | page = 81
}}</ref> Deltoidal icositetrahedron and [[deltoidal hexecontahedron]] are two Catalan solids with kite faces only.{{sfnp|Williams|1979|p=[https://archive.org/details/geometricalfound00will/page/93 93]}}

== Dimensions and angles ==
=== Dimensions ===
The deltoidal icositetrahedron with long body diagonal length ''D'' = 2 has:
*short body diagonal length:
::<math>d = \frac{2 \sqrt{3} \left( 2 \sqrt{2} + 1 \right) }{7} \approx 1.894\,580 ;</math>
*long edge length:<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Deltoidal Icositetrahedron |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/DeltoidalIcositetrahedron.html |access-date=2022-10-06 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}<br />In this MathWorld entry, the small rhombicuboctahedron has edge length <math>a = 1 ;</math> so this s.r.c.o.h. has circumradius <math>R = \frac{ \sqrt{5 + 2 \sqrt{2}} }{2}</math> and midradius <math>\rho = \sqrt{1 + \frac{ \sqrt{2} }{2}} ;</math> so this s.r.c.o.h.'s dual with respect to their common midsphere is the deltoidal icositetrahedron with inradius <math>r _{ _{ a = 1 } } = \frac{ \rho ^{2} }{R} = \sqrt{ \frac{ 2 \left( 7 + 4 \sqrt{2} \right) }{17} } = \sqrt{2}</math>×<math>\sqrt{ \frac{7 + 4 \sqrt{2}}{17} } = \sqrt{2}</math>×<math>r _{ _{ D = 2 } } .</math></ref>
::<math>S = \sqrt{2 - \sqrt{2}} \approx 0.765\,367 ;</math>
*short edge length:<ref name=":0" />
::<math>s = \frac{ \sqrt{20 - 2 \sqrt{2}} }{7} \approx 0.591\,980 ;</math>
*inradius:<ref name=":0" />
::<math>r = \sqrt{ \frac{7 + 4 \sqrt{2}}{17} } \approx 0.862\,856 .</math>

<math>r</math> is the distance from the center to any face plane; it may be calculated by [[Plane (geometry)#Operations##Distance from a point to a plane|normalizing]] the equation of plane [[Deltoidal icositetrahedron#Cartesian coordinates|above]], replacing (''x'', ''y'', ''z'') with (0, 0, 0), and taking the [[absolute value]] of the result.

A deltoidal icositetrahedron has its long and short edges in the ratio:
:<math>\frac{ S }{ s } = 2 - \frac{1}{ \sqrt{2} } \approx 1.292\,893 .</math>

The deltoidal icositetrahedron with short edge length <math>s</math> has:
*area:<ref name=":0" />
::<math>A = 6 \sqrt{29 - 2 \sqrt{2}}\,s ^{2} ;</math>
*volume:<ref name=":0" />
::<math>V = \sqrt{122 + 71 \sqrt{2}}\,s ^{3} .</math>

=== Side Lengths ===
In a deltoidal icositetrahedron, each face is a kite-shaped quadrilateral. The side lengths of these kites can be expressed in the ratio 0.7731900694928638:1.
Specifically, the side adjacent to the obtuse angle has a length of approximately 0.707106785, while the side adjacent to the acute angle has a length of approximately 0.914213565.

== Occurrences in nature ==
The deltoidal icositetrahedron is a [[crystal habit]] often formed by the mineral [[analcime]] and occasionally [[garnet]]. The shape is often called a trapezohedron in mineral contexts, although in [[solid geometry]] the name [[trapezohedron]] has another meaning.

== Related polyhedra ==
The deltoidal icositetrahedron's projection onto a [[cube]] divides its squares into quadrants. The projection onto a regular [[octahedron]] divides its equilateral triangles into kite faces. In [[Conway polyhedron notation]] this represents an ''ortho'' operation to a cube or octahedron. 

The deltoidal icositetrahedron <small>(dual of the [[Rhombicuboctahedron|small rhombicuboctahedron]])</small> is tightly related to the [[disdyakis dodecahedron]] <small>(dual of the [[Truncated cuboctahedron|great rhombicuboctahedron]])</small>. The main difference is that the latter also has edges between the vertices on 3- and 4-fold symmetry axes <small>(between yellow and red vertices in the images below)</small>.

=== Dyakis dodecahedron ===

A variant with [[pyritohedral symmetry]] is called a '''[[dyakis dodecahedron]]'''<ref>[http://loki3.com/poly/isohedra.html#24k Isohedron 24k]</ref><ref>[http://metafysica.nl/isometric.html The Isometric Crystal System ]</ref> or '''diploid'''.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20130918103121/https://www.uwgb.edu/dutchs/symmetry/xlforms.htm The 48 Special Crystal Forms]</ref> It is common in [[crystallography]].<br>A dyakis dodecahedron can be created by enlarging 24 of the 48 faces of a disdyakis dodecahedron. A [[tetartoid]] can be created by enlarging 12 of the 24 faces of a dyakis dodecahedron.
[[File:Perfect_diploid.stl|thumb|3D model of a dyakis dodecahedron]]<ref>Both is indicated in the two crystal models in the top right corner of [[:File:Modèles cristallographiques-Musée de minéralogie de Strasbourg.jpg|this photo]]. A visual demonstration can be seen [[c:Category:Disdyakis polyhedra untruncated (light and dark brown)#Transitions|here]] and [[c:Category:Tetartoid (light and dark brown)#Transitions|here]].</ref>

=== Stellation ===
The [[great triakis octahedron]] is a stellation of the deltoidal icositetrahedron.
